title: Auth cache invalidation race causing token-quota mismatch and 429 flood - retrospective
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production incident on 2025-02-13 produced widespread 429 responses (~30 minutes) for a subset of authenticated clients. Root cause was a race between per-node auth policy cache invalidation and quota reconciliation: some gateway nodes used stale policy that removed a recently-granted token exemption while others used refreshed policy, causing token owners to be inconsistently evaluated and hit quota enforcement simultaneously. This triggered a '429 flood' that cascaded into downstream retries and increased upstream load. This ticket captures timeline, technical root cause, immediate mitigations, and consolidated action items for prevention and detection.
timeline: 2025-02-13T11:03Z - First spike of 429s observed on synthetic canaries and customer dashboards (latency ~5s, error rate ~18%).
2025-02-13T11:08Z - On-call paged; initial hypothesis: quota configuration change.
2025-02-13T11:15Z - Investigated recent deploys; noticed PR #5124 (auth-policy-delta) rolled out 10 minutes earlier.
2025-02-13T11:24Z - Confirmed inconsistent auth-cache versions across gateway nodes (some still serving pre-deploy policy).
2025-02-13T11:30Z - Temporary mitigation: throttling of aggressive retrying clients and manual promotion of refreshed policy to lagging nodes via orchestration job.
2025-02-13T11:45Z - Full convergence observed; 429 rate returns to baseline by 11:50Z.
root_cause: Auth policy refresh is eventually-consistent across gateway nodes. The code path that removes a token exemption performs a non-atomic local cache eviction and emits a best-effort background reconciliation. Under the recent deploy timing and load profile, ~40% of nodes still evaluated old policy while others evaluated new policy that re-applied quota checks. Token-based quotas are enforced locally per node; the mismatch allowed the same token to be treated as exempt on some nodes and quota-eligible on others, producing sudden quota bursts when traffic hit the nodes that had enforcement enabled. The orchestration lacked an atomic rollout handshake or short fence period for critical token changes.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back part of PR #5124 to prevent new token exemption removal behavior from propagating further.
Triggered a forced cache invalidation job across all gateway replicas (orchestration job: infra/job/force-auth-cache-20250213).
Applied temporary soft-limit increase for affected token groups to absorb in-flight requests.
Added temporary traffic shaping rules to reduce simultaneous retries from clients identified by IP and token hashes.
long_term_actions: Implement atomic policy rollout mechanism: centralized versioning + gate that ensures all gateways load version N before switching enforcement (design doc: confluence.redwood/gateway-policy-rollout).
Migrate token-exemption state to authoritative store (Redis with compare-and-swap / lease) and change local cache to subscribe to invalidation events via pub/sub.
Change quota enforcement to consult a lightweight coherence check when token exemption events occur (short-circuit to central store for critical tokens for 5 minutes after a change).
Add canary sequencing for policy deploys (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on increased 429 rate relative to baseline.
action_items: ENG-20012 - Design and implement centralized policy versioning and handshake (owner: Luca Moreno, estimate 8).
ENG-20035 - Replace best-effort cache eviction with Redis-based invalidation + pub/sub listeners (owner: Priya Desai, estimate 5).
ENG-20048 - Instrument and alert: add metric 'auth.policy.convergence_seconds' and an on-call alert when >60s (owner: Soren Li, estimate 2).
ENG-20051 - Add quota-violations spike dashboard and SOM (signal-of-malice) to console and markbook runbook (owner: Observability team, estimate 3).
ENG-20066 - Run chaos tests simulating staggered policy refresh across gateways and validate no 429 spike (owner: Reliability eng, estimate 3).
verification_plan: Unit + integration tests for pub/sub invalidation logic with simulated network partitions.
Staged rollout: canary to 5% of traffic for 24h with synthetic load and compare 429s to control group.
Post-deploy smoke: run token-exemption change script and assert <1% variance in enforcement across nodes within 30s.
Run load replay of customer traffic from 2025-02-13 while feature flags enabled to validate stability.
notes: Customer communication: support drafted 'incident summary' for affected customers; CS outreach prioritized for top-10 impacted tenants.

This incident is distinct from previous quota cache bugs we saw in 2024 — that one involved stale quota counters (ENG-17521). The key difference here is a stale auth-policy (exemption state) rather than stale counters.
We observed increased client retries that amplified the flood; client-side retry guidelines need reinforcement in SDKs (see SDK-121).
